name: finished
meaning: The command finished and no row failed. Without --check, every answer ends here, including no and not sure. With --check, decide takes one text and succeeds when its answer is yes; filter succeeds when at least one of its records answers yes.
when: Every row answered or was not sure. With --check: the single decide answer was true, filter kept at least one record, a choose answer was given, or find found a line.

next.title: Use the answer as an exit code

name: no
meaning: With --check, no record answered yes and none was not sure.
when: Only with --check on decide, filter, choose or find.

next.title: Use the answer as an exit code

name: usage
meaning: An argument, option, setting or key is wrong or missing, or a single text input is empty or blank. No record was judged.
when: A usage error stops the call before any row returns.

name: not sure
meaning: With --check, no record answered yes and at least one was not sure.
when: Only with --check, when an answer fell inside the --low and --high band.

next.title: Thresholds and the not sure band

name: backend
meaning: A service error stopped the call before it produced any result, such as a refused key.
when: A call-level service error. A produced failed result always exits 6.
noExample: A service may refuse the whole call before producing a result, such as when authentication is rejected. Check the key and account. A produced failed result uses exit 6 instead.

name: local
meaning: A local failure stopped the call: a file could not be opened or written, or a toolbox could not be read.
when: A local or internal error raised for the call.

name: failed rows
meaning: The command finished, and one or more rows failed. The other rows still hold their answers.
when: Any result has status failed, including a service outage affecting every message. A failed result wins over every --check verdict.

name: interrupted
meaning: The command was interrupted with Ctrl-C or SIGINT. A second interrupt exits at once.
when: The first interrupt cancels input, backend work and run children.

name: broken pipe
meaning: The program reading the output closed the pipe before the command finished writing.
when: A downstream command such as head exits early. Under set -o pipefail the pipeline returns 141 too, so set -e stops the script.
